newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica gold stocks edge firmer, industrials knocked.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica gold stocks edge firmer, industrials knocked.

text.p: South African gold shares ended marginally firmer on Wednesday on the back of a bullish gold price and a steady rand, dealers said.
But industrial shares took a knock on the back of profit-taking and a recent spate of poor company results reported by some industrial heavyweights.
The yellow metal stood around the $353 level for most of the day, while the rand hovered around the 4.43 level against the dollar.
Dealers said market sentiment remained upbeat ahead of the budget on March 12.
The industrial index closed 46.7 points down at 8,378.8 while the gold index gained 4.9 points to 1,543.4, leaving the overall index 2.9 points higher at 7,205.7.
They said volumes of about 821 million rand were traded towards the close at around 1425 GMT.
Dealers expected trade to be sound on Thursday provided there were no nasty surprisers from a host of financial statistics due out throughout the day.
January trade data is scheduled for release at 0800 GMT on Thursday, followed by trade, fourth quarter gross domestic product, January inflation, money supply and credit extension figures.
Near-dated gold share futures ended firm, but off their highs as bullion staged a marginal recovery and industrial contracts retreated on a weaker rand and long bonds.
The March gold contract was at 1,087/95 from 1,095, the industrial contract at 8,080/90 from 8,216 and the all-share contract at 6,555/58 from 6,601.
